triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a mere generalization and could not: the pre-fix `section_122_component_rate` version [2026-02-24, 2026-07-23] zeroed the 10% surcharge whenever `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b`, flags the same commit reveals to be China-301 list-1/2024-action and §232-aluminum membership (the 301 component's `entry_is_line_a`/`entry_is_line_b` become `entry_is_china_301_list123`/`entry_is_china_301_2024_action`, and the aluminum component's `entry_is_line_b` becomes `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`). Reading the cited proclamation through the pinned release (us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-02-25/2026-03824) settles it: paragraph 14 exempts an enumerated product-category exclusion list (Annexes I/II) plus "(k) all articles and parts of articles currently or that later become subject to additional import restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232" — and nothing keyed to section 301 membership. So the exemption reached the wrong population of entries (all 301-listed lines, of every origin) while missing the population the source exempts (all exclusion-list products and all §232-covered metals, not just aluminum), which is exactly what the fix's `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered` gate restores. The §122 proof atoms are byte-identical pre and post, so nothing here is excerpt/provenance bookkeeping; the encoded meaning changed.

triage.verifier_notes: Refutation attempts and what survived: (1) "mechanical" fails — five rule formulas change condition tokens and a new derived rule plus a stack term are added; (2) "not_a_defect / new coverage" fails for the flagged rule_path, though it is the right verdict for the co-located `section_232_steel_component_rate` + `ch27_s232_steel_heading_rate` addition (the PR says the witness's ferroalloy exemplar sits outside note 16(c), so this is coverage the module never claimed — a reviewer should not count the steel half as a defect); (3) "unclear" fails because the source text is explicit and the PR names the behavior "unlawfully suppressed". Kind is the only genuinely contestable part: `untraceable_branch` ("formulas grounded on the wrong provision") is a near-tie, since §301 list membership has no basis in the §122 proclamation and the fix re-grounds the branch. I kept wrong_entity_or_scope because the proof atoms show the old proxies did trace to the right provision for the witness's own lines (the exclusion-list excerpt "7202.11.10" is line a; line b is a 232-covered aluminum line) — the failure is that those line-specific proxies select the wrong entry population once the module claims chapter-wide scope, which is also how the PR states the harm ("on §301-member lines for all origins"). Either kind would be defensible; the fidelity classification itself is solid (~0.9). Corpus-hygiene flag: this is a machine-generated composition module (generator bump b1.6-schedule-compositions-2 → -3, hand edits prohibited) and the identical §122 re-gating appears in all 100 generated chapter modules in this commit, so it is one generator defect replicated 100×, not 100 independent defects. Side note, not load-bearing: the atom citing "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04" to us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-230 did not resolve to that text in the pinned release (page-230 there is the §232 steel TRQ note), a possible pagination drift worth a separate look; it is unchanged by this diff.
